DayLeaf Terms of Service

Journal and screening results

You can log symptoms, medication use and daily activities and complete PHQ-9, GAD-7, C-SSRS self-reports and DBT worksheets. Scores and summaries reflect what you record. They do not diagnose a condition, predict safety, prescribe treatment or establish a clinical relationship. Discuss results and medication questions with a qualified clinician. A saved dose entry is not an instruction to take or change medication.

Safety plans and sharing

No one monitors your entries or screening answers through DayLeaf. Saving a safety plan, recording a request for support or completing a screen does not alert a clinician, emergency service or other contact. If you need immediate help, contact local emergency services directly. You decide whether to call a contact or share a report. A Doctor Summary or SSDI function summary is your self-report. It does not certify disability, replace agency forms or medical evidence, or submit a claim.

Private records and exports

Your journal and drafts are encrypted in this browser. Keep the password and a separate encrypted .dat backup. There is no publisher password-recovery service. Clearing browser data can erase the journal. Review dates, included screens and worksheets, names and recipients before sharing. Printed pages and exported PDFs contain readable health information. Protect those copies and never post them in a public issue or repository.

Use of records and software

You keep whatever rights you have in your records and exports. Enter, import and share only material you are authorized to handle. Use the software lawfully. Do not falsify records, use another person’s credentials without permission, or interfere with others’ access. Do not send private records to a public project channel.
